sentence: This project studies which bacteria and archaeal microbes live in hot springs by reading whole genomes taken from samples.
This project tries to find out where heat comes from and how much flows through the seafloor, using a shipboard survey and rock sampling.
This project tries to find chemical mixtures that stop ice crystals from forming in cells and are less toxic to cells.
This project studies how short circuits change high-frequency waves traveling through high-voltage transmission lines so faults can be detected.
This project builds devices where superconductors touch gold or graphene and searches for signs of non-trivial topology using electrical measurements.
This project tries to find out how a subtropical seagrass could spread into higher latitudes of the western Atlantic coast and replace eelgrass.
This project tests how two long-lived tundra plant species are affected by environmental change and rare climate events, using transplants and long-term monitoring.
This project studies how mammal tails evolved, how they develop, and how the shape, size and number of vertebrae affect how a tail is used.
This project uses machine learning tools to read news reports and measure which rebel or government groups control local areas in conflict zones over time.
This project studies how to join ethylene with polar monomers into plastics, using a photocatalyst and visible light to break open stable chelates.
This project studies silicon nanocrystals joined to organic radical compounds to see how light creates spin states useful as qubits.
This project tries to find out how simple a surface can be when it maps into different spaces under set constraints.
This project looks at a farm management system that uses artificial intelligence to control light, temperature, humidity and nutrients inside greenhouses.
This project builds a computer vision system that helps make processing decisions about forest products under changing light, blocked views and vibration.
This project builds 3D printed soft robots that use fluidic logic, flexible channels and flexible electronics to move through confined spaces.
This project builds theory that explains how AI systems forget old tasks when they learn new ones, and how knowledge carries over between tasks.
